findings.reason: a worker whose base reproduction shows acceptance cannot then produce a control whose red log reads the bare line, so it either falsifies the control or blocks; the control has to name the base behaviour it actually produces, as the reproduction clause already does.
findings.text: §16's negative control states unconditionally that removing the revision comparison "makes the first case read the bare line again", while the same done-when's reproduction clause now records what the base revision does "verbatim, whether it refuses with the bare line or accepts it"; the deliverable repeats the presumption with "in place of the bare `command_matches_suite_command` line", and the code supports the accepting branch, because `_arm_missing_fields` already accepts the command resolved at the arm's own recorded revision (`_scoped_suite_command(record, revision=revision)`, promotion_records.py:722–725) — so a mid-run arm whose command matches its own revision's resolution is accepted today, and the control's stated red log would be unattainable

findings.reason: a worker holding the declared scope cannot satisfy the "every repair advice" clause without editing a file it was not granted, so the deliverable must either add `reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py` to the write paths and name `_repair_resume_advice`, or narrow the clause to the resume advice `resumption.py` composes.
findings.text: §15's deliverable requires that "Every resume or repair advice the crew composes" name both revisions, but its write paths name only `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` and `reckon/crew/resumption.py`, and the repair advice is composed by `_repair_resume_advice` in `reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:750` (called at :1713); `resumption.py` holds the resume prompt writer and the refused-advice store, not the repair composer, so the section names no file for half its deliverable
